messages:
alex: Thinking out loud — I want to propose a lightweight preemptive-prefetch signal from the scheduler into the allocator. Problem: short microbatches repeatedly trigger GPU->host page faults that add 10-30ms tail latency.
meera: +1 can you sketch the signal surface? e.g., how scheduler tells allocator which pages will be hot?
alex: Rough idea: when a request is accepted, scheduler emits a hint list of page ranges (or model shard ids) that will be touched. Allocator exposes prefetch_hint({tenant, model_id, ranges}, deadline_ms) which is best-effort.
joan: Are we talking about a synchronous prefetch (blocking) or async warm path? We should avoid blocking the critical path.
alex: Async warm path only. Prefetch returns a token and the runtime can await token if it prefers. Default flow: fire-and-forget; latency-sensitive routes can await.
dmitri: Two concerns: (1) how do we avoid thrashing on competing tenants? (2) how do we account cost? We already have admission tokens for staging.
meera: For tenant fairness we can tie prefetch hints to existing admission tokens and score them against tenant quota. If quota exhausted, hints are downgraded to lower priority background prefetch.
joan: Implementation detail: allocator needs an efficient representation — suggest namespace by (tenant, model_variant) and compact range descriptor. Also add a max-prefetch-per-epoch to avoid overfetch.
alex: Agreed. Example API sketch:

prefetch_hint(tenant="acme", model="gpt-small-v2", ranges=[{shard:3, start:0, len:64}], deadline_ms=20) -> hint_token
await hint_token.wait(timeout_ms)

infra-bot: deploy-bot: perf/job-1723 started — we should be careful introducing non-deterministic background IO.
dmitri: Another tradeoff: prefetch can increase memory pressure. Suggest allocator expose a drop callback so hint can be canceled under memory pressure.
meera: Also add telemetry: hit/miss for hints, avg wait time, and memory reclaimed due to canceled hints. That will drive tuning.
joan: Operationally, we can gate this behind a feature flag per pool and run a canary on low-traffic hosts.
alex: Next steps: I'll draft an RFC with API surface, admission integration, and telemetry. @meera @dmitri if you can add perf targets (e.g., 50% reduction in fault tail p99 for small-batch chat) that'd be great. :thumbsup:
meera: I can do that, will pull existing microbatch traces and set target numbers tomorrow.
dmitri: I'll try a quick prototype in the allocator branch — won't land until RFC + canary.
alex: cool, will start RFC. Thanks all. :rocket:
